title: Market Terminal — Bloomberg ANSI Command Grid
description: A three-panel Bloomberg-terminal layout stacking monospaced ticker tables, a full-width sparkline, and ANSI-glyph status indicators on a dense black ground — built for signal density, not decoration.
philosophy: This template borrows the visual grammar of professional trading screens: amber-on-black contrast ratios tuned for sustained reading, character-cell precision that makes every glyph load-bearing, and a strict horizontal panel hierarchy that the eye learns in seconds. It refuses gradients, illustration, and any whitespace that isn't structurally earned. It exists for rooms where the audience already knows what the numbers mean and needs to find anomalies fast — not be introduced to data storytelling.
goodFor: Live market or real-time data read-outs in fintech demos
Internal quant, data-engineering, or SRE team reviews
Hackathon pitches centered on dense technical metrics
Trading platform product walkthroughs showing feed fidelity
avoidFor: Executive narrative decks requiring warmth and breathing room
Consumer-facing pitches where accessibility and visual comfort matter
Slides carrying a single headline and a hero image
Contexts with WCAG contrast compliance requirements for projected text
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The title slide feels like a trading terminal session initializing — cold, purposeful, the suspended beat before market open. The deck name appears as though typed at a command prompt rather than designed as a headline, lending it the authority of a system command rather than a marketing statement. Compositional rhythm is rectilinear and grid-locked throughout, with ANSI box-drawing characters forming hard structural borders rather than decorative frames; the overall mood is signal-ready and infrastructural. Avoid any warmth, curvature, softness, or whitespace that isn't load-bearing — nothing here exists to welcome, only to orient.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed dark ground, zero decorative margin — all edges are structural. 12-col grid: title block occupies cols 1–8, left-anchored at the character-cell baseline; cols 9–12 hold a right-panel stub of static ANSI-glyph status indicators or a frozen ticker column. A single-row status bar pins the top (session ID, date stamp area), and a command-prompt band locks the bottom — these two rails bracket the entire vertical composition. Hierarchy is achieved purely through weight contrast and monospaced column alignment; no rule lines are added because the character grid itself acts as the structural rule.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a live terminal mid-session — oppressively dense, ruthlessly utilitarian, no pixel wasted on ornament. High-contrast glyphs and hairline rule lines create a left-to-right scan rhythm across stacked data bands, with no single zone allowed to dominate. Hierarchy emerges from character density and glyph weight rather than scale contrast, keeping all three panels in visual equipoise. Avoid softness, gradients, curvature, or any whitespace not structurally earned by the grid.
